item.title: Minute's silence observed in Seanad for former Minister Paddy Cooney
item.description: A minute's silence has been observed in the Seanad for former cabinet minister Paddy Cooney, from Athlone. The Longford-Westmeath politician served in several ministerial roles in the 1970s and 80s. He died last Saturday at the age of 94, and his funeral will take place in Athlone tomorrow. He was also a senator for four years, and Senator Padraic Brady paid tribute to his Fine Gael colleague in the Seanad: Advertisement

item.title: Local calls for Garda body-cams to be rolled out
item.description: A public consultation on how and when gardaí should wear body-cams has been launched. The force is looking for feedback on a code of practice for the devices, which can help investigate and prosecute criminals. The cameras, which are attached to clothing, are already being piloted at five garda stations in the east and south. item.title: Two men charged over alleged Athlone assault
item.description: Two men arrested have been arrested in connection with an alleged assault in Athlone. The two men, one in his 20s and one in his late teens were detained at Athlone Garda Station under section 4 of the Criminal Justice Act 1984. Following the incident on Gleeson Street, two other men were hospitalised with what are believed to be minor injuries. item.title: Local hospital introduce visiting restrictions
item.description: Sligo University Hospital is urging people with flu-like symptoms not to visit the hospital, as flu cases continue to rise sharply in the community. The hospital is currently managing two flu outbreaks on separate wards and is treating 27 patients with confirmed flu. Since the start of the flu season, 193 cases have been confirmed in Sligo, with 56 last week alone. Advertisement Eighty people have been hospitalised so far, including 20 last week. item.title: Serious concern over shortage of therapists for children with disabilities
item.description: Serious concerns have been raised about the shortage of therapists, for children with disabilities, in Roscommon and Galway. It's after the government announced plans to cut waiting lists for children hoping to get assessed. Parents who believe their child has autism will also be encouraged to avail of a new autism assessment launching in February. But Sinn Fein TD Claire Kerrane told the Dáil it won't solve the recruitment problem: Advertisement

item.title: Ballinamore motorcyclist died in crash with van during hailstorm, inquest hears
item.description: A Ballinamore motorcyclist died in a crash with a van during a heavy hailstorm, according to an inquest today. The coroner recorded a verdict of accidental death. 49-year-old Andrew Mitchell, from Derradda, Ballinamore, died after coming off his Honda Moped at Aghacashlaun, Drumcong, Co Leitrim, on March 3, 2022, at around 5 o’clock in the evening. item.title: Emergency services currently at the scene of crash near Mullingar
item.description: Gardaí and emergency services are currently at the scene of a road traffic collision in County Westmeath. The collision occurred this afternoon on the N4 in Ballinalack near Mullingar. There are reports of heavy traffic and local diversions are currently in place. More to follow.... Advertisement

item.title: Power Restored to Over 100 Homes in South Leitrim
item.description: Power has now been restored to over 100 homes in the south Leitrim area, according to the ESB. 139 customers in the Gorvagh area were left without electricity following Storm Bram yesterday. It had been estimated that power wouldn't be restored until tomorrow afternoon. Advertisement According to ESB Powercheck, however, the fault was fixed just before two o'clock today.

item.title: Local TD Accuses EU of Stripping Ireland of its Power
item.description: A local TD has accused the EU of stripping Ireland of its power in a strongly worded Dáil speech. Roscommon-Galway TD Michael Fitzmaurice said recent trade agreements, including Mercosur, are unfair and driven by larger EU states such as Germany. Fitzmaurice argued that directives like the habitats directive have "tied the country in knots" and undermined national control. item.title: Man airlifted to hospital after being seriously injured in Ballinalack crash
item.description: A man has been airlifted to a Dublin hospital in a serious condition after a crash between a truck and a car in Co Westmeath, near the Longford border. The two vehicles collided on the N4 at Ballinalack shortly after 1.30 this afternoon. The driver of the car, a male in his 40s, was brought by air ambulance to the Mater Hospital in Dublin and has since been transferred to Beaumont Hospital, where he remains in a serious condition.
